front: Weight components for slope angle α to the horizontal, positive downhill and perpendicular outwards?
back: $F_\parallel=+F_G\sin\alpha$, $F_\perp=-F_G\cos\alpha$. In the right triangle of force vectors, the parallel component is opposite $\alpha$ and the perpendicular component is adjacent. At $\alpha=0^\circ$, $F_\parallel=0$; as $\alpha\to90^\circ$, $F_\perp$ tends to zero. Different axes may change the signs, not the physical directions.

front: Dry friction: when can a contact stick, and which friction force acts?
back: Let $N$ be the magnitude of the contact normal force. Sticking is possible while the required tangential magnitude satisfies $F_\mathrm{required}\le\mu_S N$. Actual static friction adjusts to that demand and opposes impending relative sliding; equality can still be a limiting case of sticking. For surfaces already sliding, $|F_R|=\mu_K N$, opposite their relative motion. The friction arrow starts at the selected body.
